title: Not every dogma needs explicit grasp; privates need not pastor-level defense
source_text: LXII. Praeterea non negant ad fidem salvificam non necessario a singulis requiri singulorum fidei dogmatum expressam, seu distinctam & explicitam apprehensionem, sed sufficere si expresse noverint fundamentalia atque praecipua fidei mysteria. Imo nequidem respectu praecipuorum istorum fidei mysteriorum necessario a privatis exigunt distinctam atque accuratam illorum intelligentiam, qua istiusmodi mysteria tueri, explicare & probare possint. Quod quidem in Doctore & Pastore necessarium est, in privato ex eorum sententia non item.
pass_a_gloss: Furthermore they do not deny that for saving faith there is not necessarily required from each person an expressed, or distinct and explicit, apprehension of every single dogma of faith, but that it suffices if they expressly know the fundamental and principal mysteries of faith. Indeed not even with respect to those principal mysteries of faith do they necessarily demand from private persons a distinct and accurate understanding of them by which they can defend, explain, and prove such mysteries. Which indeed is necessary in a Doctor and Pastor; in a private person, on their view, not likewise.
pass_b_english: Reformed do not require from every believer explicit apprehension of every dogma; knowing fundamental principal mysteries expressly is enough.
Even for those principal mysteries, privates need not the distinct accurate intelligence by which doctors and pastors defend and prove them.
